newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 31.

text.p: The following are the top stories in the Irish press on Tuesday.

- With BUPA Ireland due to start trading in the Irish market tomorrow, the state health insurer VHI has rejected compromise proposals designed to remove any legal uncertainty about the plans on offer by the British health insurer.

- With the confirmation af two more cases of BSE in Ireland, one in Louth and one in Monaghan, eight counties have now exceeded the acceptable level of incidence of the disease set by Russia when announcing its selective ban on the importation of Irish beef in October.

- There has been a fall in the number of companies which became insolvent during the year and the trend is expected to continue in 1997, according to figures published yesterday by the Irish Trade Protection Association (ITPA).

- Figures released by the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) today are expected to show a fall of five percentage points in the Irish debt/GDP ratio during 1996 on the back of a booming economy and strong Irish pound.
- Warnings of a big freeze at New Year, with bitterly cold weather and snow, were issued by Met Eireann.
- BUPA Ireland is confident that the Department of Health will give it permission to begin seeking business here tomorrow.
